method: 14 sampled frames across the clip; final native frame additionally inspected for shots 08 and 12; AVFoundation decode and audio level checks.
observations: One airborne phone ends in Riley's right hand; the stranger remains separate rather than directly handing it over.
The phone initially rises on screen, then drifts toward the palm and is caught around 2.6–3.0 seconds.
limitations: The initial rise reads more like a toss or float than a clean accidental drop.
The hand and phone move too slowly together to clearly establish superhuman reflexes. The requested fast snap at 1–1.3 seconds did not land.
This remains a motion test, not a solved reflex shot.
Review used 14 sampled frames plus technical decoding; no full real-time playback or independent listening review. Native audio is preserved and needs sound-design/mix review.
